summary.revenue: Total revenues were $17,823 million for Q2 2024, up from $16,623 million in Q2 2023. Adjusted premiums, fees and other revenues were $13,523 million, down 1% on a reported basis and up 1% on a constant currency basis from the prior-year period.
summary.eps: Net income per share was $1.28, up 167% from $0.48 in Q2 2023. Adjusted earnings per share were $2.28, up 18% from $1.94 in Q2 2023.
summary.guidance: Not disclosed. The document does not provide explicit forward guidance for revenue, earnings, or growth.
summary.margin: Expense ratio was 17.9% for Q2 2024, compared to 17.7% in Q2 2023. Adjusted expense ratio, excluding total notable items related to adjusted other expenses and PRT, was 20.6% for both periods.
key_risks: Net investment losses of $421 million, primarily driven by normal trading activity in the portfolio.
Net derivative losses of $508 million, largely driven by the U.S. dollar strengthening and an increase in long-term interest rates.
Book value per share decreased 5% from $34.92 to $33.30, and book value excluding AOCI other than FCTA decreased 1%.
RIS adjusted earnings decreased 2% due to lower recurring interest margins.
MetLife Holdings adjusted earnings decreased 27% primarily due to the reinsurance transaction completed in 2023.
Chilean encaje returns were lower in Latin America, partially offsetting growth.
key_opportunities: Group Benefits adjusted earnings up 43% driven by favorable underwriting, particularly in life.
RIS sales up 62% year-to-date, driven by UK longevity reinsurance and $3.5 billion in pension risk transfer deals.
Asia adjusted earnings up 8% on a constant currency basis, driven by favorable underwriting and higher variable investment income.
Latin America adjusted earnings up 8% on a constant currency basis, driven by strong volume growth and favorable underwriting.
EMEA adjusted earnings up 20% on a constant currency basis, driven by volume growth and higher recurring interest margins.
Holding company cash and liquid assets of $4.4 billion, above the target cash buffer of $3.0-$4.0 billion.
